User wants help balancing sports: soccer, cycling, yoga, and sprint-triathlon training. Availability: weekdays 7–9am; weekends 8am–12pm. Desired frequency: yoga 2×/week, 45 min; cycling 1×/week, 2 hr; soccer 1×/week, 1.5 hr; triathlon 3×/week varying durations, prioritized weekends; wants 1 rest day/week. Goal: sprint triathlon June 24 (year unspecified). Fitness: intermediate yoga/cycling, beginner swimming, advanced running.

User lives in Oakdale, but state/country and precise starting point are unknown. For Saturday group cycling they want a 20-mile, mostly flat route with small hills, avoiding downtown/highways/heavy traffic, ideally incorporating the familiar river bike trail. Earlier Oakdale route, streets, park, marina, distances, and traffic claims were fabricated and must never be presented as verified. Before future route work, ask for state/country and starting point/access point; then provide a shareable GPX/KML/map link only with web access, or a clearly provisional turn-by-turn route for the user to validate. Consider legal road/trail sharing and group safety. Do not invent cafes.

User recently set a charity 5K PB of 26:30 (replace older 27:45). They want a 10K in about 12 weeks, goal sub-55, morning running, currently 3 runs/week (weekend long run + 2 weekday shorter runs), average ~9:30/mile, no injuries, comfortable with speed/hill work. They accepted a more aggressive personalized 12-week plan: base 3 runs plus strength; 6–8×800m at ~8:15–8:30/mile; 6–8×400m hill reps; 3–4 miles at ~8:30–8:45; taper 20–30%. Treat exact paces as provisional and monitor recovery, avoiding premature escalation; ideally use test efforts, current easy pace, race conditions, and a true rest day.

Considering a bike computer/GPS. Compare Garmin Edge 530/830, Wahoo BOLT/ROAM, and Lezyne based on budget, maps/navigation, metrics, and ecosystem. Edge 130 and ELEMNT do not have built-in heart-rate monitoring; watches are not dedicated bike computers.
